neighbours.label: the word piece ' perpet' / ' appet' (perpetuate, perpetually, appetite, appetising), against near-synonyms without those pieces
fire: Such rules only perpetuate the problems they were meant to solve.
The old dispute seemed to continue perpetually across generations.
After the long hike, the children had a huge appetite for dinner.
The smell from the bakery was very appetising on a cold morning.
Low wages tend to perpetuate poverty in rural regions.
The investors showed little appetite for further risk this year.
He was perpetually late to meetings, which annoyed his boss.
The cook arranged an appetizing plate of cheese and fruit.
quiet: Such rules only prolong the problems they were meant to solve.
The old dispute seemed to continue endlessly across generations.
After the long hike, the children were very hungry for dinner.
The smell from the bakery was very tempting on a cold morning.
Low wages tend to deepen poverty in rural regions.
The investors showed little interest in further risk this year.
He was always late to meetings, which annoyed his boss.
The cook arranged a tasty plate of cheese and fruit.
